title: Airgap Packaging and Day-2 Hardening for Private Deployments
author: Maya Thompson
content:
Summary:

This document describes the recommended artifact packaging, offline transfer processes, and operational hardening for Redwood Inference private deployments in airgapped or strongly restricted network environments. It covers the end-to-end: build artifact composition, signing & verification, offline bundle creation, installation checklist, Day‑2 operations (patching, backups, monitoring), and a conservative upgrade + rollback pattern tailored to on‑prem and VPC private deployments.

Scope and audience:

- Scope: On‑prem and VPC private deployments that cannot access public registries at install time (airgapped) or that require signed offline bundles for compliance. Includes interaction points with KMS, audit logging, and customer-managed registries.
- Audience: Solutions engineers, delivery engineers, platform reliability engineers, and customer SREs performing installation, upgrades, or maintenance of private Redwood deployments.

Key goals:

1) Provide reproducible, verifiable offline installation bundles for airgapped installs.
2) Ensure secure artifact signing and provenance (SBOM + signatures).
3) Minimize blast radius for Day‑2 operations and enable safe rollbacks.
4) Provide clear troubleshooting and recovery steps for common failure modes.

Prerequisites (customer / deliverable):

- Hardware profile (recommended):
  - Controller nodes: 2x vCPU, 8GB RAM (small installs) or 8+ vCPU and 32+GB RAM (production control plane).
  - Worker (runtime) nodes: GPU hosts per committed shape; general-purpose nodes: 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM for sidecars and runtime orchestration.
  - Disk: 200GB root + 1TB ephemeral recommended for model caching.
- Network: internal DNS resolution, private NTP, HTTPS restricted egress allowed to a customer approval endpoint only for license activation (optional).
- Security: KMS/HSM endpoint (if using customer-managed keys), customer firewall rules allowing intra-cluster traffic on TCP 443, 10250-10255 (container runtime), and agent heartbeats on UDP 8125 (default).
- Delivery artifacts from Redwood: signed offline bundle .tar.gz, manifest.json, signed SBOM (.spdx.json + .sig), installation guide, and a lightweight bootstrap container image if mirror registry not available.

Artifact packaging and contents:

Each offline bundle produced by Redwood is composed of the following files (manifest-driven):

- bundle-<version>-<yyyyMMdd>.tar.gz  (primary archive)
- manifest.json  (SHA256 hashes for each contained file, schema v1)
- sbom.spdx.json  (SBOM for all images and binaries)
- sbom.spdx.json.sig  (Ed25519 signature of SBOM)
- signatures.tar  (collection of artifact signatures, GPG or Ed25519)
- images/  (OCI tarballs or image archives for redwood-controller, redwood-runtime, redwood-agent, redwood-ops-gateway)
- charts/  (Helm charts pre-rendered for the target cluster distro)
- configs/  (example YAMLs: installation values.yaml, kms-mapping.yaml, storage-class.yaml)
- scripts/  (offline registry mirror script, bundle-verify.sh, install.sh)

Manifest example (human-readable snippet):

| filename | sha256 | size_bytes | type |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| images/redwood-controller_v1.8.2.tar | <hash> | 12345678 | oci_image |
| charts/redwood-helm-1.8.2.tgz | <hash> | 234567 | helm_chart |

Signing and verification:

- All bundles are signed with Redwood release keys. Delivery includes public verification keys and the key fingerprint.
- Installation step must run scripts/bundle-verify.sh which checks manifest hashes and verifies signatures against the included public keychain. Failure to verify must abort install.
- SBOM must be checked for prohibited components (policy: no inbound telemetry binaries). Use provided sbom-lint rules to enforce customer policy.

Offline registry strategies (choose one):

1) Customer mirror registry: recommended for larger installs. Steps:
   a) Use images/* tarballs with provided mirror script to load images into the private registry (OCI).
   b) Update values.yaml with registry overrides and pull secrets.
   c) Run helm install using the chart tarballs pointing to the private registry.

2) Local image load (single host bootstrap):
   a) For constrained environments, load OCI tarballs into the local container runtime (ctr or docker load) on each node via secure media.
   b) Use DaemonSet helper that ensures local images are present before startup.

Installation checklist (high level):

1) Verify host pre-reqs: OS packages, kernel modules, disk layout, NTP.
2) Transfer bundle via approved media (sftp within secured network, thumb drive handed by authorized personnel, or secure airgap transfer service).
3) Run bundle-verify.sh and examine manifest + SBOM.
4) Mirror images to private registry or load locally per chosen strategy.
5) Apply values.yaml with customer-specific KMS endpoints, storage classes, node selectors, and networkPolicy overrides.
6) Helm install redwood-controller + redwood-runtime with --wait and 10m timeout.
7) Post-install smoke tests: control-plane API responds, agent heartbeats observed, a small inference request (local model) completes < 5s.

Day‑2 operational hardening:

- Patch management:
  - Strategy: OS security patching on a rolling window with node cordon/drain. Apply patches to non‑runtime nodes first (control plane), then to runtime nodes in controlled batches.
  - Recommended cadence: monthly security patch window; emergency CVE patching within 72 hours for critical CVEs.
- Model cache & disk: monitor /var/lib/redwood/cache usage. Configure eviction thresholds: warn at 70%, critical at 90%.
- Secrets and keys: integrate with customer KMS. For airgapped KMS, pre-provision a vault-mounted key and configure kms-mapping.yaml. Rotate keys yearly or per customer policy; test rotation in staging bundle first.
- Networking hardening: enforce NetworkPolicies for namespaces. Default deny except for explicit control-plane <-> runtime ports.
- Logging & metrics:
  - Ship logs to customer ELK/Graylog or S3-compatible endpoints.
  - Promote metrics: redwood_request_latency, redwood_model_cache_hit_ratio, agent_heartbeat. Alerting thresholds: 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 5m, agent_heartbeat missing > 2m triggers P1.
- Audit logging: all install/upgrade actions must record operator identity, bundle fingerprint, and timestamp to the cluster audit log.

Upgrade and rollback pattern (airgapped-aware):

Principles: keep upgrade artifacts deterministic, minimize on-disk migration, and ensure an automatic safe-fail mechanism that reverts to the previous Helm release and images if health checks fail.

Planned upgrade steps:

1) Prepare a verification bundle in staging and run a full smoke and regression test set (automated) using the same offline install procedure.
2) Produce an upgrade bundle: contains new images and a delta manifest listing only changed images and charts. Sign and deliver to customer.
3) Prestage images in private registry or load them to nodes ahead of running the upgrade window.
4) Execute upgrade: helm upgrade --timeout 15m --wait --install redwood-controller charts/redwood-helm-<new>.tgz -f values.yaml --set imagePullPolicy=IfNotPresent
5) Health checks performed by orchestrator: control-plane API readiness, agent heartbeats, model-serving readiness for a set of canonical prompts. If any health check fails for > 10m, automatically run rollback script.

Rollback script behavior (automated):

- helm rollback redwood-controller <previous_revision>
- Reapply previous images if the orchestrator replaced images during upgrade.
- Recreate any deleted persistent volumes from snapshots (see backup procedure).

Backup and restore recommendations (Day‑2):

- Control-plane backup: etcd snapshot cadence daily with off-node storage (S3-compatible or NFS). Retain 14 snapshots. Test restore quarterly.
- Model cache backups: not mandatory; models are considered ephemeral. However, if customers pin local-only models, snapshot the model storage weekly.
- Configuration backup: store values.yaml and manifest.json versioned in a customer SCM repository.

Troubleshooting quick reference (common failure modes):

- Failed bundle verification: check signature fingerprint, ensure public verification key matches the key in the delivery email, rerun bundle-verify.sh.
- Images fail to load into registry: inspect registry logs for permission denied; verify registry certificates and pull secrets.
- Helm install times out: inspect pods for CrashLoopBackOff; describe pod and check events for PVC or image pull errors.
- Agent heartbeats missing: verify agent logs (/var/log/redwood-agent.log), check firewall rules for agent -> controller port, validate node clock skew.

Operational runbook (short):

1) Incident detection: alert triggers (missing agent heartbeat, control-plane unhealthy).
2) Triage: collect logs (controller, agent, kubelet), run redwood-diagnostic.sh (bundled script) and upload tarball to customer incident bucket.
3) Mitigation: if a single runtime node fails, cordon + drain, redeploy runtime pods to healthy nodes. If control-plane degraded, promote standby controller and roll back recent changes.
4) Postmortem: attach bundle fingerprint and operator identity to postmortem record.

Ownership and contact points:

- Delivery owner: Solutions Engineering (primary contact in delivery ticket).
- Oncall: Customer SRE (first responder) then Redwood Platform SRE escalation (pager duty team: Redwood‑Private‑SRE).
- Release artifacts and signatures: release-ops@redwood.ai (include fingerprint in subject).

Appendices:

A. Example install commands (offline):

- Verify bundle:
  ./scripts/bundle-verify.sh /opt/offline/bundles/bundle-1.8.2-20260210.tar.gz
- Mirror images to registry:
  ./scripts/mirror-to-registry.sh --bundle images/ --registry registry.internal.corp:5000 --auth /etc/registry/creds.json
- Install helm charts:
  helm install redwood-controller charts/redwood-helm-1.8.2.tgz -f configs/values.yaml --wait --timeout 600s

B. Minimum acceptance smoke tests:

- control-plane /health returns 200 within 5s
- redwood-agent heartbeat metric appears within 60s of agent restart
- small inference (local model) returns consistent answer in < 5s

C. Security notes for compliance reviewers:

- Keep offline bundle fingerprint in customer evidence repository.
- All delivery media must be hand-signed and transferred under chain-of-custody process for high-security customers.

If you need a tailored checklist for a specific OS distro, on-prem virtualization platform (VMware, OpenShift), or custom KMS/HSM integration, attach requests to the delivery ticket and Solutions Engineering will produce a customer-specific addendum.
